module_title: Important Days and Dates - Foundational and High-Frequency Global Days
introduction: Important Days and Dates represent one of the most reliable scoring topics under the Static GK umbrella. Almost every competitive one-day exam (SSC, Railways, State Exams) contains at least one direct date-matching question. This foundational level targets the globally celebrated calendar milestones that every candidate must know.

core_concepts.title: International Women's Day (March 8)
core_concepts.description: Celebrated globally to recognize women's social, economic, cultural, and political achievements, while acting as a focal point in the movement for women's rights.

core_concepts.title: World Environment Day (June 5)
core_concepts.description: Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 1972 during the Stockholm Conference, it serves as the principal vehicle for inspiring global awareness and action for environmental protection.

core_concepts.title: International Day of Yoga (June 21)
core_concepts.description: Inaugurated by the UN in 2015 following an initiative by India. June 21 corresponds to the Summer Solstice, the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere, which holds significant spiritual context in yoga.

core_concepts.title: World Health Day (April 7)
core_concepts.description: Marks the founding anniversary of the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1948. It is used annually to draw global attention to a specific major theme of global health.

core_concepts.title: World AIDS Day (December 1)
core_concepts.description: Instituted in 1988, this day is dedicated to raising awareness of the AIDS pandemic caused by the spread of HIV infection and mourning those who have died of the disease.

important_entities.name: March 8
important_entities.significance: Dedicated to accelerating gender parity and celebrating female trailblazers.

important_entities.name: June 5
important_entities.significance: The UN's flagship day for promoting global ecosystem restoration.

important_entities.name: June 21
important_entities.significance: Global recognition of the ancient Indian physical, mental, and spiritual practice.

important_entities.name: December 1
important_entities.significance: The Red Ribbon serves as the universal symbol of awareness and support for this day.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Nature Trap: Environment vs. Earth Day
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Candidates frequently cross-wire 'World Environment Day' and 'Earth Day'. Remember clearly: Earth Day is celebrated on **April 22**, whereas World Environment Day is celebrated on **June 5**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Associate the word 'March' as an action directly with International Women's Day on March 8.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct date matching (Match the Following) is the most common question format for this level. Prioritize memorizing these core 15–20 global dates until they become second nature.
